title: Algebraic Fractions: Simplify, Multiply, Divide, Add and Subtract
seo_title: Sec 2 Algebraic fractions Worksheets: Free Secondary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: multiplication and division of simple algebraic fractions; addition and subtraction of algebraic fractions with linear or quadratic denominator
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 maths worksheets on algebraic fractions: simplifying by factorising, multiplying and dividing, and adding and subtracting with number and linear denominators. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Factorise first, then cancel common factors, never single terms.
key_sub: To add or subtract, use a common denominator and put brackets round each numerator.
body_html:
How it works

  • Algebraic fractions follow the same rules as number fractions.
  • To simplify, factorise the top and bottom, then cancel common factors (never single terms).
  • To multiply, multiply tops and bottoms and cancel. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
  • To add or subtract, use a common denominator, multiply each top to match, then combine. Put brackets round each top so a minus sign changes every term.
Example

Simplify x² − 9x + 3.

x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3)

Cancel (x + 3)

Answer: x − 3

Example

Simplify x + 12 − x − 35.

Common denominator 10

5(x + 1) − 2(x − 3)10 = 5x + 5 − 2x + 610

Answer: 3x + 1110

Example

Simplify 2x + 3x + 1.

2(x + 1) + 3xx(x + 1)

Answer: 5x + 2x(x + 1)

Common mistakes

  • Cancelling terms: x + 6x + 2 is not 3.
  • Adding straight across: 1x + 1y is not 2x + y.
  • Forgetting to multiply every term in the bracket when making a common denominator.
  • Losing the minus sign: −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6.

faq.q: How do you simplify an algebraic fraction?
faq.a: Factorise the numerator and the denominator fully, then cancel any common factors. Only whole factors can be cancelled, not single terms.

faq.q: How do you add algebraic fractions?
faq.a: Find a common denominator, rewrite each fraction over it, then add the numerators. Simplify the answer if possible.

faq.q: How do you divide algebraic fractions?
faq.a: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second, then cancel common factors.

faq.q: Why can't I cancel the x in (x + 6)/(x + 2)?
faq.a: Because x is a term added to 6, not a factor of the whole numerator. Cancelling only works when the same factor multiplies the whole top and bottom.

items.q: Arjun drives 40 km at x km/h and then 60 km at (x + 15) km/h. Which expression gives the total time in hours?
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed: 40x + 60x + 15 = 40(x + 15) + 60xx(x + 15) = 100x + 600x(x + 15).
